summary: Measure the visual width of a string in terminal columns, with a Rust core.
description: Returns how many columns a string occupies in a terminal. CJK characters and most emoji take two columns, combining marks and zero-width characters take none, and ANSI escape codes are ignored. CLI tools use it to align tables, progress bars, and prompts.
A drop-in alternative to string-width 9.0.0 with the same API and results, plus a batch API. It runs as a native addon in Node.js and as WebAssembly in browsers.
compatibility: Same API, options, defaults, and results as string-width 9.0.0.
The original's own test suite (466 tests) passes unchanged.
Identical results on every Unicode code point, every RGI emoji sequence, and 200,000 random strings, for every option combination.
differences: Uses Unicode 17.0 tables, while the original follows the Unicode version of the runtime (Node.js 22.23 and 24.21 both use Unicode 17.0).
The browser build must be initialized once with init() before use.
Short ANSI-colored ASCII strings are slower than with the original: crossing into Rust costs more than the work.

benchmarkHighlights.label: 1,000 CLI table cells (80% plain ASCII), batch API
